title: Daryl Hannah in "Blade Runner" isn't discussed enough.

commenti.body: She injured her arm severely shooting that one scene with Sebastian when she crashed into the car. Didn’t even flinch. That take is the one that made it to the film and you would never guess she was hurt if you didn’t know. That’s true commitment. She was a great actress. She was great in the Invisible man too.

Many note the influence of the Fritz Lang/Thea Von Harbou film *Metropolis* (1927) on *Blade Runner*.

That film is often called the great-granddaddy of science fiction films because… it is.  *So many* elements from that film would find themselves in other science fiction works!

However, what many don’t know quite as well is that the Lang/Von Harbou team followed up *Metropolis* with *Spione* (1928), what many consider the great-granddaddy of *spy* films.  In fact, watching it today, even though the pace is much slower than modern films, there are so many classic spy movie tropes to be found in *Spione* I can’t help but think author Ian Fleming *must* have seen the film before writing his James Bond novels.

What does this have to do with *Blade Runner* and, specifically, Daryl Hannah’s role in the film?

Glad you asked.

There’s this scene in *Spione* where the evil female spy, realizing the Japanese diplomat she wants to get close to for nefarious reasons, often passes by a certain block on his way home.  She goes to the place he passes and grabs some newspapers and makes herself look destitute and when the diplomat passes, she acts surprised when he almost bumps into her.  He feels sorry for her and takes her to his place and tragedy ensues…

…sound familiar?

Yup.

Ridley Scott *absolutely* stole the whole Pris meeting Sebastian bit from *Spione*…!

I love her death scene. It truly feels like she’s a malfunctioning machine on the verge of breaking down, rather than a human being made of flesh. I also like how she tries to kill Deckard, she wants to kill but doesn’t really know how. Everything about her physical performance shows that she was created solely as a sexual object and is now attempting to kill a man using the limited programming she has.
The first time I watched Blade Runner when I was young...that death scene was pretty disturbing...
Wow, never looked at it that way.

You mean “Memoirs of an Invisible Man”? Elisabeth Moss was in “The Invisible Man” (2020), which is a reboot of the 1933 film starring Claude Rains. 

“Memoirs of an Invisible Man” and “The Invisible Man” are two different books and films. They’re not related.
Yes of course the John Carpenter movie, but you already knew that since I mentioned Daryl Hannah. I couldn’t remember the title at the time.

When she auditioned she came in a DIY costume that was punk and quirky. Then when she came in she saw the other girls had much sexier interpretations. She suddenly got embarrassed but obviously they liked her style.
I believe you but that's just too much of trope isn't it, even in books.

Is it though?

Again, in both *Spione* and *Blade Runner* the “bad guy” lady makes herself look destitute.  Uses discarded newspapers as a makeshift “blanket” around herself.  The victim/mark walks by (something the bad guy lady knows), she acts surprised/terrified and seemingly fears being beaten or rousted by this person (adding to her looking very much a victim of this cruel world) and tries to “run away” (part of the act to gain sympathy).  The victim feels sorry for her and takes her in… which results in tragedy for him.

I genuinely cannot think of another movie or book I’ve read where such a sequence of events happen in that sort of order.
